Studio / Styles / Café Terrace at Night

Café Terrace at Night

Vincent van Gogh, 1888

Oil on canvas

Lamp-lit café terrace under a starry blue sky, in warm yellows and oranges.

Use this style

Vincent van Gogh, Café Terrace at Night, 1888. Kröller-Müller Museum, Otterlo. Source on Wikimedia Commons. Licence: Public domain.

About the painting

Van Gogh painted this café on the Place du Forum in Arles in September 1888, working outside at night. Writing to his sister, he said he wanted to paint a night picture without any black, using only blue, violet and green, with the lit square in pale sulphur yellow and citron green.

It is the first painting in which he shows a starry sky, a year before The Starry Night. The gas-lit yellow awning and terrace glow against the deep blue street, and the cobblestones are painted as small, separate dabs. It is in the Kröller-Müller Museum in Otterlo, in the Netherlands.

How it looks on your photo

Photos warm up with yellow and orange light set against blue shadows, with short, textured strokes. It is a good choice for streets, buildings and evening photos, and a gentler alternative to The Starry Night.
